column1: # Driver inventory for tests/stdlib/. CLOSED INVENTORY.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# Review found that the gate validated `.pd -> golden` and never `golden -> .pd`
# or `manifest -> disk`. Deleting tests/stdlib/stdlib_tail_return.pd — the single
# driver this whole gate exists for — left an orphaned golden and a GREEN run.
# A gate that gets weaker when you delete its most important fixture is not a
# gate. Phase 2 enforces three-way set equality between:
#     this file  ==  *.pd on disk  ==  *.expected on disk
# so deletion, renaming, an orphaned golden and an undeclared driver are all red.
# SEAM: transcript verification of these drivers belongs to `make conformance`,
# whose runner has an expected-output verdict class and its own closed inventory
# over tests/. This file does NOT re-diff transcripts; it pins the inventory and
# the expected verdict of the GENERATED-C structural check.
# Columns (tab-separated): basename  golden  cverdict  purpose
# cverdict — what scripts/check-generated-c.sh must say about this file's C:
#   clean                       the invariant holds; a violation is a REGRESSION
#   known_violation:<fn>[,<fn>] the invariant is EXPECTED to be violated, in
#                               exactly these functions, because of an open
#                               compiler defect. Fewer, more, or different
#                               functions all fail the gate — an expectation
#                               that cannot go stale. If the violation vanishes
#                               the gate reports XPASS and this entry must be
#                               promoted to `clean`.
stdlib_tail_return

column4: D3 IS ONLY HALF FIXED. A tail `if` is never lowered to a return, so a function ending in if/else still miscompiles silently. Pins the open defect; promote to `clean` when the parser lowers tail `if`.
